a: Threadmark watches specific channels you choose — no one else. It captures the outcome of a conversation, not every message. Every entry is confirmed by a real teammate before it appears in the knowledge base, so people stay in control of what gets published.

q: How do you handle private channels and DMs?
a: Private channels and DMs require the explicit consent of every participant before anything is published. Threadmark asks privately, never shares the original messages, and publishes only a redacted summary. If anyone declines, nothing leaves the room.

q: How is this different from searching Slack?
a: Slack search finds threads. Threadmark finds answers. When you ask 'why do we retry webhooks 3 times?', you get a confirmed decision with context, author and date — not a list of threads to read through. Old answers are marked replaced so you never act on stale information.

q: What happens when an entry is wrong?
a: Any team member can flag, edit or replace an entry. Old entries are marked as replaced and kept for the audit trail — never deleted. The person who confirmed the original entry is notified so nothing changes without visibility.
